title: Luminescence Dating
description: Quartz grains in a pot or a hearth stone are dosimeters. Firing empties their electron traps; afterwards the trace radioactivity of the soil fills them again, at a steady rate. Heat or light the grains in the laboratory and they glow with what they stored: the dose since the fire, divided by the yearly dose, is the age. Unlocks the Luminescence Reader.

puzzle.goal: A sherd has received an equivalent dose De since it was fired, at an annual dose rate Ḋ. Write its age A.
puzzle.name: The luminescence age
puzzle.ask: Find A in thousands of years for De = @{De} Gy and Ḋ = @{Dr} Gy per thousand years.
puzzle.method: The traps fill at a steady rate since the firing: the dose stored is the rate times the time.
